title: Embodied Consciousness & Neural Computation
subtitle: Deep Dive Audio Series • Clinical Coma Mysteries, Biophysics & Living Neurons vs. AI

sections.heading: Words, Phantoms, Memory & Dreams: Clinical & Historical Mysteries of Consciousness

episodes.label: When Stroke Steals Words vs. Meaning — Broca's 'Tan,' Sign-Language Aphasia & Inner Silence
episodes.notes: Traces Broca's 1861 autopsy of Leborgne (and 2007 3T MRI re-scanning), Salk Institute ASL stroke dissociations, corollary discharge, and anendophasia.

sources.title: Broca (1861) & Dronkers et al. (2007, Brain)
sources.detail: High-resolution 3T MRI of Leborgne and Lelong's preserved brains revealing deep arcuate/superior longitudinal fasciculus lesions

sources.title: Poizner, Klima & Bellugi (1987)
sources.detail: What the Hands Reveal About the Brain — left-hemisphere sign aphasia vs. right-hemisphere visuospatial neglect in native ASL signers

sources.title: Nedergaard & Lupyan (2024, Psychological Science)
sources.detail: Anendophasia: experimental profile of healthy adults lacking an inner monologue

episodes.label: Julian Jaynes on Trial — Did Bronze Age Humans Hear Gods Before Inventing 'I'?
episodes.notes: Puts Julian Jaynes's 1976 Bicameral Mind hypothesis on philological and neurobiological trial against Homeric Greek, Middle Kingdom papyri, and corollary-discharge fMRI.

sources.title: Jaynes (1976) & Snell (1953)
sources.detail: Homeric vocabulary of thymos, phrenes, kardia, and psyche in the Iliad

sources.title: Dispute Between a Man and His Ba (~1900 BCE, Papyrus Berlin 3024)
sources.detail: Middle Kingdom Egyptian interior dialogue refuting late-1200 BCE invention of introspection

sources.title: Ford & Mathalon (2005) / Sommer et al. (2008)
sources.detail: Frontotemporal efference-copy failure and right-hemisphere homolog activation in auditory verbal hallucinations

episodes.label: Ghosts in the Cortical Map — Civil War Phantoms, Penfield's Probe & Mirror Boxes
episodes.notes: From S. Weir Mitchell's Gettysburg amputees and Wilder Penfield's awake cortical mapping to Ramachandran's mirror box, aplasic phantoms, and somatoparaphrenia.

sources.title: Mitchell (1866 / 1872, Injuries of Nerves)
sources.detail: Turner's Lane Hospital Civil War clinical series coining 'phantom limb'

sources.title: Penfield & Boldrey (1937, Brain)
sources.detail: Somatic motor and sensory representation in the cerebral cortex of awake surgical patients

sources.title: Ramachandran & Rogers-Ramachandran (1996, Proc. R. Soc. B)
sources.detail: Synaesthesia in phantom limbs induced with mirrors and cortical remapping

episodes.label: Seven Seconds of Now — Patient H.M., Clive Wearing & How Memory Stitches Time
episodes.notes: Unpacks Henry Molaison's 1953 medial temporal resection, Brenda Milner's mirror-star dissociation, Clive Wearing's 7-second diary, and hippocampal time cells.

sources.title: Scoville & Milner (1957, JNNP) & Annese et al. (2014, Nature Comms)
sources.detail: Loss of recent memory after bilateral hippocampal lesions and 2,401-slice histological reconstruction of H.M.'s brain

sources.title: Wearing (2005) & Sacks (2007, Musicophilia)
sources.detail: Clive Wearing's HSV-1 encephalitic amnesia sparing polyphonic conducting and emotional recognition

sources.title: Eichenbaum (2014, Nature Reviews Neuroscience)
sources.detail: Time cells in the hippocampus bridging temporal gaps across conscious episodes

episodes.label: The Dreaming Brain Unparalyzed — REM Behavior Disorder & Two-Way Lucid Signals
episodes.notes: From Michel Jouvet's pontine atonia switch and Schenck's REM Behavior Disorder alpha-synuclein prodrome to real-time eye-signal dialogues inside verified REM sleep.

sources.title: Jouvet & Michel (1959) / Valencia Garcia et al. (2017)
sources.detail: Sublaterodorsal tegmental glutamatergic-to-medullary glycinergic circuit enforcing REM spinal paralysis

sources.title: Schenck, Mahowald et al. (1986 / 2013, Sleep Medicine)
sources.detail: Isolated REM sleep behavior disorder converting >80% to Parkinson's, DLB, or MSA over 10–15 years

sources.title: Konkoly, Paller, Arnulf, Dresler et al. (2021, Current Biology)
sources.detail: Real-time two-way arithmetic and Morse eye-movement dialogue during PSG-confirmed REM lucid dreaming

episodes.label: Where Does Pain Actually Live? — Anzio Beachhead, Nav1.7 & Predictive Interoception
episodes.notes: Debates peripheral nociceptive specificity (Nav1.7 SCN9A) vs. top-down insular predictive interoception (Beecher at Anzio, 1995 boot-nail case, naloxone placebo blockade).

sources.title: Beecher (1946, Annals of Surgery) & Fisher et al. (1995, BMJ)
sources.detail: Anzio beachhead wound analgesia vs. severe agony from a 15 cm boot nail that missed the foot entirely

sources.title: Cox et al. (2006, Nature)
sources.detail: SCN9A Nav1.7 loss-of-function mutations causing complete congenital insensitivity to pain

sources.title: Levine, Gordon & Fields (1978, Lancet) & Craig (2009)
sources.detail: Naloxone reversal of placebo analgesia and anterior insula interoceptive synthesis

episodes.label: Before the Brain Had a Name — Egyptian Hearts, Aristotle's Radiator & Herophilus
episodes.notes: How humanity spent 2,000 years locating mind in the heart or diaphragm—from Edwin Smith's trauma papyrus to Aristotle, Herophilus in Alexandria, and Galen's laryngeal pig.

sources.title: Edwin Smith Surgical Papyrus (~1600 BCE, Cases 6, 20 & 22)
sources.detail: Earliest hieroglyphic word for brain (ais), molten-copper gyri, and temporal crush speechlessness

sources.title: Aristotle (Parts of Animals II.7) vs. Hippocratic On the Sacred Disease
sources.detail: Cardiocentric brain-as-radiator model vs. cephalocentric seat of consciousness

sources.title: Von Staden (1989, Herophilus: The Art of Medicine in Early Alexandria) & Galen
sources.detail: 3rd-century BCE human cadaveric dissection of sensory/motor nerves and Galen's recurrent laryngeal nerve demonstration

episodes.label: Wine-Dark Seas & Unspeakable Odors — How Language Shapes Color, Smell & Bedside Pain
episodes.notes: From Gladstone's 1858 shock over Homer's color words and Berlin & Kay's hierarchy to Jahai abstract odor vocabulary and cross-cultural bedside pain ideophones.

sources.title: Gladstone (1858) & Berlin & Kay (1969, Basic Color Terms)
sources.detail: Luminance-vs.-hue vocabulary in Homeric Greek and cross-linguistic color lexicalization

sources.title: Majid & Burenhult (2014, Cognition)
sources.detail: Odors are expressible in language, as long as you speak the right language (Jahai hunter-gatherers)

sources.title: Winawer et al. (2007, PNAS) & Imai / Kita
sources.detail: Categorical color perception and Japanese mimetic clinical pain ideophones (zukizuki, chikuchiku, jinjin)

episodes.label: Babylonian Neurology vs. Cos — Esagil-kin-apli's 1050 BCE Seizure Tablet & Hippocrates
episodes.notes: Reads Neo-Babylonian Sakikkū Tablet XXVI (~1050 BCE) side-by-side with Hippocrates's On the Sacred Disease (~400 BCE): Jacksonian marches, auras, and post-ictal paresis.

sources.title: Kinnier Wilson & Reynolds (1990, JNNP / Brain 2014)
sources.detail: Translation and neurological semiology of British Museum Neo-Babylonian Sakikkū Tablet XXVI on miqtu / epilepsy

sources.title: Esagil-kin-apli (~1050 BCE, Borsippa)
sources.detail: Editorial colophon weaving the 40-tablet Diagnostic Handbook

sources.title: Hippocratic Corpus (~400 BCE, On the Sacred Disease)
sources.detail: Naturalistic attack on temple purifiers paired with humoral phlegm-in-veins pathophysiology

episodes.label: Dream Surgery at Epidaurus — Asclepian Sleep Temples, Sacred Snakes & Placebo Neurobiology
episodes.notes: Walks into the 4th-century BCE abaton at Epidaurus—translating the carved Iamata stelae alongside archaeological scalpels and modern PAG opioid/CB1 imaging.

sources.title: Edelstein & Edelstein (1945) / LiDonnici (1995)
sources.detail: The Epidaurian Miracle Inscriptions (Iamata Stelae A & B) — Kleo, Ambrosia of Athens, Pandaros, Aeschines

sources.title: Hart (2000) & Archaeological Museum of Epidaurus
sources.detail: Excavated bronze surgical scalpels, forceps, and Zamenis longissimus / temple-dog wound licking (histatins & lysozyme)

sources.title: Benedetti (2014) & Wager / Zubieta (J. Neurosci)
sources.detail: PET/fMRI proof of prefrontal-to-PAG mu-opioid and CB1 cannabinoid release during therapeutic ritual

episodes.label: Alkaline Lithium Springs & Unchained Asylums — Soranus of Ephesus & Humane Roman Psychiatry
episodes.notes: How Soranus of Ephesus (~100 CE) condemned chains, darkness, and the 'wandering womb' myth while prescribing cognitive rehabilitation and lithium-rich alkaline waters.

sources.title: Soranus of Ephesus via Caelius Aurelianus (On Acute and Chronic Diseases)
sources.detail: 2nd-century CE Methodist protocol banning chains, whipping, and dark dungeons in mania and melancholia

sources.title: Soranus (Gynecology I & III)
sources.detail: Anatomical refutation of Plato's 'wandering womb' (hysteria) via cadaveric uterine ligament attachments

sources.title: Cade (1949, Medical Journal of Australia) & Jefferson
sources.detail: Rediscovery of lithium salts in mania 1,800 years after Soranus's northern Italian alkaline spring prescriptions

episodes.label: Strasbourg 1518 & the Dancing Plagues — Rye Ergot Alkaloids vs. Mass Motor Contagion
episodes.notes: Debates Claviceps purpurea ergot alkaloid pharmacology vs. famine-and-curse predictive dissociative trance in the July 1518 Strasbourg Dancing Plague.

sources.title: Strasbourg Municipal Council Archives (July–Sept 1518) & Paracelsus (1526)
sources.detail: Frau Troffea's six-day silent dance, magistrate-hired guild stages, and St. Vitus shrine pilgrimage at Saverne

sources.title: Waller (2009, The Dancing Plague / Lancet)
sources.detail: Archival reconstruction of 1515–1517 Rhine famine, St. Vitus curse terror, and culturally scripted dissociative trance

sources.title: Eadie (2003) & Edwards et al. (2012, Brain)
sources.detail: Convulsive vs. gangrenous Claviceps purpurea ergotism vs. Bayesian active-inference models of functional motor disorders

episodes.label: Evolved for the Impossible — Bajau 13-Min Divers, Denisovan Sherpas & 13.7 °C Survival
episodes.notes: How genetic evolution (Bajau PDE10A giant spleens, Denisovan Sherpa EPAS1) and Q10 thermodynamics (Anna Bågenholm's 13.7 °C resuscitation) shield the 20W human brain.

sources.title: Ilardo, Moltke, Korneliussen, Nielsen et al. (2018, Cell)
sources.detail: Physiological and genetic adaptations to diving in Sulawesi Bajau sea nomads (PDE10A-driven 50% spleen enlargement)

sources.title: Huerta-Sánchez et al. (2014, Nature) & Horscroft et al. (2017, PNAS)
sources.detail: Altitude adaptation in Tibetans caused by introgression of Denisovan-like EPAS1 (HIF-2α) DNA

sources.title: Gilbert, Busund, Skagseth, Nilsen & Solbø (2000, Lancet)
sources.detail: Resuscitation from accidental hypothermia of 13.7 °C with 80-minute circulatory arrest and full neurological recovery
